ana: Capturing questions from today's all-hands people ops segment — drop follow-ups here. @erica and @jamal will answer live, and I'll note items we need follow-ups on.

mike: Quick one — what's the official promotion cadence for ICs vs managers? I remember hearing twice a year but confused about ad-hoc promos.

erica: Short answer: formal cycles are March and Sep. Ad-hoc promotions are allowed for exceptional cases (high-impact hiring, retention risks). We use the leveling rubric + manager recommendation + peer feedback. Typical weight: manager assessment ~60%, peer/skip-level ~30%, and measurable outcomes ~10%. Docs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/People/Promotion-Guide

jamal: To add — when we do ad-hoc promos we still put candidates through the same rubric and the comp committee reviews for budget impact. Most ad-hoc promos are small in number and need a sponsor from leadership.

sophie: How transparent are salary bands per level? Can managers share the band mid-career conversations?

erica: Bands are visible to managers and people ops; we encourage sharing the midpoint/range with ICs during leveling conversations. We don't publish a public spreadsheet, but you'll get band info in 1:1 if you ask. If you'd like, DM me and I'll share the band for your level.

mike: If someone is promoted in-cycle, when does the comp change hit payroll? Next cycle or immediate?

jamal: Promotions processed before payroll cutoffs get applied the next pay run. If it's after cutoff, it's applied the following cycle. For larger promo-driven comp adjustments we sometimes do retro pay if approval spans pay periods.

erica: Also important: equity refreshes are handled separately and are not automatic with a promotion, but they are often discussed together. We route refresh/grant requests to the comp committee and 1:1 with manager helps set expectations.

sophie: Any update on leveling calibrations? I heard some teams wanted clearer examples for L4->L5.

erica: We're drafting new example-impact writeups for common IC career paths (infra, infra-ml, platform, product). Expect a PR to the handbook this week with concrete before/after examples. We’ll post a summary in #eng and link here.

hr-bot: Reminder — promotion nominations window for the March cycle: 2025-03-01 to 2025-03-14. Submit via /promo-nom or the Promotions form.

mike: Thanks, useful. One more: does time-in-role minimum still apply? I thought it was 9 months.

erica: We prefer 9 months as a guideline for non-exceptional promos. Exceptions happen but need stronger evidence of sustained impact and leadership sponsor.
